path.description: The absolute path of a text file to read content from

start_line.description: Optional one-based starting line number to read from; use null or omit for the start of the file

end_line.description: Optional one-based ending line number to read through; use null or omit to read to the end of the file or the read cap, whichever comes first

items.description: A file read request with optional inclusive one-based line bounds. Always include path; start_line/end_line must be on the same object as the path they apply to, never in a separate array element

files.description: Array of file read requests; each element is one file and must include path. Omit start_line/end_line or set them to null to read from the start; provide integers on the same object as the path to return only that inclusive one-based line range — never emit a range as its own array element. Reads are capped, so page through long files with start_line/end_line. Prefer this tool over running terminal command to get file content for better performance and reliability.

queries.description: Array of regex search queries to execute

path.description: The absolute path for the action to be performed on

old_text.description: Exact text to replace (must match exactly once). Omit this when creating a missing file or inserting via insert_line. Keep this at or below 6000 characters when possible; larger payloads should be split across multiple tool calls to avoid timeouts.

new_text.description: The new content to write when creating a missing file, the replacement text for edits, or the inserted text when insert_line is provided. Keep this at or below 6000 characters when possible; for large edits, use multiple calls with small chunks of old_text and new_text to iteratively edit the file.

insert_line.description: Optional positive one-based boundary line. When provided, the tool inserts new_text before that line instead of performing a replacement edit; use line_count + 1 to append at EOF.

inputSchema.description: Edit a text file by replacing old_text with new_text, create the file with new_text if it does not exist, or insert new_text at insert_line when insert_line is provided. Prefer using this tool for file edits over shell commands. IMPORTANT: large edits can time out, so use small chunks and multiple calls when possible.

question.description: The single question to ask the user. E.g. "How can I help you?"

options.description: Array of 2-5 user-selectable answer options for the single question

input.description: A patch in the *** Begin Patch / *** End Patch envelope.
